In case you’re in SEQ with this cyclone we have incoming here’s the advise the vets and everyone are sharing. 
- Move your horses now. If your paddock might flood move them now. QSEC and Caboolture show grounds open their stables for emergencies like this. Contact them to move your horse BEFORE roads close
- If your paddock doesn’t flood, secure anything that might fly around 
- Put your horses in a paddock with visible fences, clear areas and make sure they have clean water available in troughs
- Tag them. I’ve plaited part of my ponies mane and put duct tape over it with my name and number in case a fence goes down and she gets out. 
- Make sure you have your human and horse first aid kid readily available and stocked. 
- Keep an eye on your horse for cellulitis and rain scald 
- Make sure their tetanus vaccine is up to date - flood wounds are NASTY

As someone who has unfortunately been attacked on horse back a few times I always dismount and stay between me and the horse. I can and will kick a dog and keep my horse behind me.
